about: Proposed region definitions for detailed maps of Argentina: 23 provinces and the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. A proposal for discussion (docs/REGIONS-AR.md); no code reads this file, and it does not ship. Most sources are national, so they are listed once under country_layers, and each region points there.

codes.why: A bare AR already means Arkansas in STATE_CODES (engine/address_search.py), and single letters mean nothing to a reader. The letter is also the first character of the Argentine postal code (CPA).
codes.verified: The ISO 3166-2 codes were not checked against the ISO site in this change.

layer_keys.crops: crops.sqlite (crop types, or land cover where no crop map exists)
layer_keys.roads: base map (OSM today); IGN roads as rural gap filler

IGN-terms.name: Términos y condiciones de uso de la información del IGN
IGN-terms.attribution: "FUENTE: Instituto Geográfico Nacional de la República Argentina"; keep update-date metadata and reuse conditions; for derived products state the date of the original IGN data; do not suggest IGN endorsement.
IGN-terms.conditions: Data must be shared freely and at no cost; commercial use only in derivative works; no use that distorts the meaning of the information.

CC-BY.attribution: Credit the Ministerio de Salud de la Nación.

Public-domain.name: Natural Earth terms of use (public domain)

terrain.notes: About 2 m vertical accuracy; heights in SRVN16; built from SRTM and ALOS, so closer to a surface model in forest and towns.

terrain.publisher: European Space Agency / Airbus Defence and Space

water.dataset: Capas SIG, "Hidrografía y oceanografía" (watercourses, canals, reservoirs, water surfaces)

water.notes: No open dam inventory found. ORSEP publishes a map of the dams it oversees, not a dataset.

crops.dataset: Mapa Nacional de Cultivos 2023/2024 (winter and summer GeoTIFF, 30 m)
crops.notes: Covers the main agricultural areas, not the whole country. Extensive crops; class mapping to build_crops.py needed. The 2024/2025 edition exists; its data and licence were not checked.

buildings.notes: Covers Latin America; inferred May 2023; Argentine coverage not measured. Licence as listed on Overture's attribution page (opened).

places.notes: Province and department codes and coordinates in the attributes.

roads.notes: As the US base map today.
Route numbers; source: Dirección Nacional de Vialidad.

addresses.notes: No Argentine address source is listed.

Each block has door-number ranges on both sides; many are 0 to 0. Files dated 2023-12-05. First-100-block sample with numbers: Buenos Aires 58, CABA 46, Jujuy 31, Corrientes 27, Córdoba 3, Chaco 3, Catamarca 1, Chubut 0, Entre Ríos 0, Formosa 0; other provinces not sampled (rate limit). Bulk file not downloaded.

addresses.publisher: Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires
addresses.notes: No licence on the file per a mirror of the record; the City's site says CC BY 2.5 Argentina. To settle with the City.

pois.dataset: Establecimientos de salud públicos (with lat/long and REFES code)
pois.publisher: Ministerio de Salud de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

pois.dataset: REFES (Registro Federal de Establecimientos de Salud), latest XLSX 2024-12-27
pois.publisher: Ministerio de Salud de la Nación
pois.notes: Licence and file list read through the CKAN API; coordinates not confirmed.

pois.publisher: Ministerio de Salud de la Nación
IGN, on the Buenos Aires province portal

postal_code.format: CPA: one letter (province, as ISO 3166-2:AR), four digits (locality, the old postal code), three letters (side of the block); the old four-digit form is still in everyday use

addressing.order: Street name, then door number, then locality and province ("Av. Corrientes 1234, C1043AAZ, Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires"); also "al 2950", corners and "entre" forms
addressing.notes: engine/address_search.py reads a postcode only as five digits and expects the number before the street; build_addresses.py would keep "C1043" from a CPA.

bbox.note: IGN's polygon follows the legal boundary (1,730 parts, to the South Pole). This box keeps the 84 parts west of 63.5° W and north of 56° S: the Argentine part of Isla Grande and Isla de los Estados. The Malvinas/Falkland Islands, the South Atlantic islands and the Antarctic sector are left to the maintainers' decision on disputed boundaries.
